newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Apr 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Apr 1.

text.p: A four-year-old girl was missing, presumed drowned, in Napier on Monday night after she, her six-year-old brother and her father were swept away by a freak wave as they walked on the beach. The three were washed out to sea. The mother tried desperately to save them but had an infant son with her. The brother and father were rescued by police and taken to Napier Hospital. Page 1.

An Auckland man who wants to initiate a referendum on replacing the Treaty of Waitangi with a constitution guaranteeing New Zealanders equal rights says he expects overwhelming support. Mark Whyte, 38, said the petition was not an anti-Maori action of any kind. "In fact I'm a great supporter of Maori. But there is a lot of racial divisiveness in our country and the root cause of a lot of it lies in the treaty." Page 1.

Property owners could be offered rate incentives and funding help to conserve historically important sites after a pending review of the Historic Places Trust. Conservation Minister Nick Smith said the review had been triggered by a critical report by the parliamentary commissioner for the environment that highlighted problems with the management, legislation and funding of historic heritage. Page 2.

A Health lobby group has called on the government to immediately free up frozen child-health funds. The government announced last year a $30 million-a-year "safety net" budget for health and disability services. But the money is off-limits for a year while the Health Ministry assesses the needs. North Health, the authority that buys services in Auckland and Northland, has described the delay as frustrating. Page 2.

The government has rejected demands by Labour that Speaker Doug Kidd improve his performance in Parliament. Last week Labour leader Helen Clark said Kidd should use Parliament's four-week recess to "reflect" on how he was going to manage Parliament when it sat again from April 22. Her comments came after an incident in which Labour deputy leader Michael Cullen was ejected from Parliament by Kidd. Page 2.

Organised crime is the most profitable enterprise in New Zealand, with earnings of about $1 billion a year, according to Labour MP Mike Moore. Moore said he was frustrated that no government agency was keeping tabs on the problem even though it was so big. Moore said the seriousness of the problem was clear from limited data that had been gathered. Page 2.

More than $500 million owed by businesses to the Inland Revenue Department should shrink as a result of new penalties in force today, IRD commissioner Graham Holland said. Holland said the debt accounted for most of the money owed to the department, and the IRD was determined to drive it down. Page 16.

Scrapping stamp duty on commercial property rather than introducing a capital gains tax should be the first step if the Reserve Bank wants a slowdown in residential property investment, the Property Investors Federation believes. Reserve Bank governor Don Brash has described New Zealand's tax laws as anomalous. Capital gains on property are not taxed, while those made by a professional fund manager or pension fund are. Page 16.
